title: Fondue
description:
Fondues are so much fun and always seem to be associated with special family times together – with the Florida families, Andrea’s birthday around Christmas or New Year’s Day, Lauren’s Birthday around Spring Break, or Mother’s Day 2009!
Everything seems festive and relatively easy and prepared just right – of course, because you get to do it just the way you like. There are, however, usually many dishes to wash if you’re at home, and that too becomes a big family get-together.
The hardest part of a fondue is deciding how much to eat, since everything is so tasty and there are usually so many varieties of foods and combinations to try. But, what the heck, it’s a party!
Here we give the outlines of some basic fondue set-ups, but there are unlimited combinations and ways to approach the meal.
Fondue
For the cheese fondues, rub inside of a 4-quart heavy pot with cut sides of garlic, then discard garlic.
Add wine (or beer) to the pot and bring just to a simmer over moderate heat.
Stir together cornstarch and kirsch (or tequila, if using; otherwise, use water or wine) in a cup.
Gradually add cheese to the pot and cook, stirring constantly in a zigzag pattern (not a circular motion) to prevent cheese from balling up, until cheese is just melted and creamy (do not let boil).
Stir cornstarch mixture again and stir into fondue (add the salsa if making the Mexican version). Bring fondue to a simmer and cook, stirring, until thickened, 5 to 8 minutes.
Transfer to the heating fondue pot.
For the broth versions, bring all the ingredients to a boil and transfer to the fondue pot.
For dipping in the cheese, use chunks of:
Crusty French bread
Apples or pears
Broccoli, cauliflower, celery, mushrooms, potatoes (blanched beforehand)
START TO FINISH: 30 MIN

Here we give the outlines of some basic fondue set-ups, but there are unlimited combinations and ways to approach the meal.

Fondue

For the cheese fondues, rub inside of a 4-quart heavy pot with cut sides of garlic, then discard garlic.
Add wine (or beer) to the pot and bring just to a simmer over moderate heat. 
Stir together cornstarch and kirsch (or tequila, if using; otherwise, use water or wine) in a cup. 
Gradually add cheese to the pot and cook, stirring constantly in a zigzag pattern (not a circular motion) to prevent cheese from balling up, until cheese is just melted and creamy (do not let boil).
Stir cornstarch mixture again and stir into fondue (add the salsa if making the Mexican version). Bring fondue to a simmer and cook, stirring, until thickened, 5 to 8 minutes.

For the broth versions, bring all the ingredients to a boil and transfer to the fondue pot.
For dipping in the cheese, use chunks of:
Crusty French bread
Apples or pears
Broccoli, cauliflower, celery, mushrooms, potatoes (blanched beforehand)

SERVES: 6 
ACTIVE TIME: 30 MIN
START TO FINISH: 30 MIN

Swiss Fondue
 1 garlic clove, halved crosswise
 1½ cups dry white wine
 1 tablespoon cornstarch
 2 teaspoons kirsch (optional)
 ½ pound Emmental cheese, 
 coarsely grated (2 cups)
 ½ pound Gruyère cheese,
 coarsely grated (2 cups)

 Mexican Fondue
 1 garlic clove, halved crosswise
 1 beer
 1 tablespoon cornstarch
 2 teaspoons Tequila (optional)
 1 pound Mexican cheese
 coarsely grated (4 cups)
 1 cup or more salsa

 Broth Fondue (better than oil)
 3 cups broth – chicken, beef, 
 vegetable, or seafood
 1 cup mixed chopped vegetables
 (mirepoix), onions, celery,
 carrots, garlic, thyme, etc.

For dipping in the broth, use chunks of:
Lobster or shrimp
Filet mignon, chicken, pork, ham, pancetta
Broccoli, cauliflower, celery, mushrooms, potatoes (blanched beforehand)
Some ideas for sauces:
Seafood cocktail sauce or melted butter
Brown gravy
Béarnaise sauce
Curry sauce (mayonnaise and curry)
Mustard sauce
Barbecue or Worcestershire sauce








For the chocolate fondue dessert, melt some dark chocolate and a little cream or corn syrup in a pan and then put it in a fondue pot, to be used for dipping:
Apples, pears, strawberries, pineapples, grapes, bananas (maybe from an edible “flower” arrangement!)
Pound cake, cheese cake or biscotti
Salted pretzel sticks
